paragraphs.english: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Dia Mirza and Adrian Grenier have a message for you: It’s easy to beat plastic. They’re part of a bunch of celebrities starring in a new video for World Environment Day — encouraging you, the consumer, to swap out your single-use plastic staples like straws and cutlery to combat the plastics crisis.
paragraphs.chinese: 阿诺德·施瓦辛格、迪娅·米尔扎和阿德里安·格雷尼尔想告诉你：战胜塑料很容易。他们与一群名人一起出演了世界环境日的新视频，鼓励作为消费者的你更换吸管、餐具等一次性塑料日用品，以应对塑料危机。

paragraphs.english: The key messages that have been put together for World Environment Day do include a call for governments to enact legislation to curb single-use plastics. But the overarching message is directed at individuals.
paragraphs.chinese: 为世界环境日汇集的核心信息，确实包括呼吁各国政府立法限制一次性塑料制品。但整体传达的重点仍是要求个人行动。

paragraphs.english: My concern with leaving it up to the individual, however, is our limited sense of what needs to be achieved. On their own, taking our own bags to the grocery store or quitting plastic straws, for example, will accomplish little and require very little of us. They could even be detrimental, satisfying a need to have “done our bit” without ever progressing onto bigger, bolder, more effective actions — a kind of “moral licensing” that allays our concerns and stops us doing more and asking more of those in charge.
paragraphs.chinese: 然而，把责任交给个人，让我担忧的是：我们对究竟需要达成什么，理解得太有限。例如，仅靠自带购物袋去超市，或不再使用塑料吸管，所能取得的成效很小，对我们自身的要求也极低。这些行为甚至可能有害：它们满足了我们“已经尽了一份力”的心理需要，却从未推动我们采取更大、更大胆、更有效的行动。这是一种“道德许可”，它让我们的担忧平息，使我们不再做更多事情，也不再向掌权者提出更多要求。

paragraphs.english: While the conversation around our environment and our responsibility toward it remains centered on shopping bags and straws, we’re ignoring the balance of power that implies that as “consumers” we must shop sustainably, rather than as “citizens” hold our governments and industries to account to push for real systemic change.
paragraphs.chinese: 当关于环境以及我们环境责任的讨论，仍围绕购物袋和吸管打转时，我们便忽略了一种权力格局：它让我们只以“消费者”的身份追求可持续购物，而不是以“公民”的身份，要求政府和产业承担责任，推动真正的系统性改变。

paragraphs.english: It’s important to acknowledge that the environment isn’t everyone’s priority — or even most people’s. We shouldn’t expect it to be. In her latest book, Why Good People Do Bad Environmental Things, Wellesley College professor Elizabeth R. DeSombre argues that the best way to collectively change the behavior of large numbers of people is for the change to be structural.
paragraphs.chinese: 必须承认，环境并非每个人最优先考虑的事，甚至不是大多数人的首要事项。我们也不该期待它必定如此。韦尔斯利学院教授伊丽莎白·R·德松布尔在新书《好人为何做出有害环境的行为》中提出，要整体改变大量人群的行为，最好的办法是进行结构性变革。

paragraphs.english: This might mean implementing policy such as a plastic tax that adds a cost to environmentally problematic action, or banning single-use plastics altogether. India has just announced it will “eliminate all single-use plastic in the country by 2022.” There are also incentive-based ways of making better environmental choices easier, such as ensuring recycling is at least as easy as trash disposal.
paragraphs.chinese: 这可能意味着实施塑料税之类的政策，让有害环境的行为付出额外成本，或彻底禁止一次性塑料制品。印度刚刚宣布，到二〇二二年将“消除国内所有一次性塑料制品”。也可以采取激励办法，让更好的环保选择更容易实现，例如确保回收至少与扔垃圾同样方便。

paragraphs.english: DeSombre isn’t saying people should stop caring about the environment. It’s just that individual actions are too slow, she says, for that to be the only, or even primary, approach to changing widespread behavior.
paragraphs.chinese: 德松布尔并不是说，人们应该停止关心环境。她的意思是，个人行动见效太慢，不能让它成为改变普遍行为的唯一途径，甚至不该是主要途径。

paragraphs.english: None of this is about writing off the individual. It’s just about putting things into perspective. We don’t have time to wait. We need progressive policies that shape collective action (and rein in polluting businesses), alongside engaged citizens pushing for change.
paragraphs.chinese: 这些主张都不是要抹杀个人的作用，而是要摆正看问题的角度。我们没有时间再等下去。我们既需要能塑造集体行动、约束污染企业的进步政策，也需要积极参与、推动变革的公民。

sentenceNotes.sentence: They could even be detrimental, satisfying a need to have “done our bit” without ever progressing onto bigger, bolder, more effective actions — a kind of “moral licensing” that allays our concerns and stops us doing more and asking more of those in charge.
sentenceNotes.structure: They 指自带袋子、放弃吸管等有限个人行为；satisfying ... 是结果或伴随说明；without ... 表示未进一步行动；破折号后名词短语概括这种心理机制，that 从句修饰 moral licensing，allays 与 stops 并列。
sentenceNotes.translation: 这些做法甚至可能有害，因为它们满足了“已尽一份力”的需要，却没推动更大胆有效的行动；这种“道德许可”平息担忧，让我们不再进一步行动或要求掌权者担责。
sentenceNotes.tip: 作者批评的是小行动带来的自我满足和停步，不是断言所有个人环保行为都无用。

sentenceNotes.sentence: In her latest book, Why Good People Do Bad Environmental Things, Wellesley College professor Elizabeth R. DeSombre argues that the best way to collectively change the behavior of large numbers of people is for the change to be structural.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: Elizabeth R. DeSombre argues that the best way is for the change to be structural.
sentenceNotes.structure: 书名为 latest book 的同位语；that 引导 argues 的宾语从句；to collectively change ... 修饰 way；for the change to be structural 是带逻辑主语的不定式结构，作表语。
sentenceNotes.translation: 德松布尔教授在新书中认为，要整体改变大量人群的行为，最好的办法是让这种改变具有结构性。
sentenceNotes.tip: for 后的 the change 是 be structural 的逻辑主语，不是受益对象。
